name: Dark Hunter Green
lede: Dark Hunter Green is a deep, blackish green, ColorHub's English name for Birōdo, a Japanese traditional color whose name means "velvet."

sections.title: A velvet color
sections.body:
The Japanese name, written びろうど and romanized Birōdo, is listed among Japan's traditional colors on Wikipedia, where it is glossed simply as "velvet" [1]. ColorHub translates it into English as Dark Hunter Green, filing it under the family of this near-black, [[hunter-green|hunter green]]-leaning shade, since "velvet" names a fabric rather than a hue a reader could picture directly [1]. The sources consulted do not say when the name was first recorded, or whether it described the color of a particular dyed velvet cloth [1].

The closest named neighbor on file is [[chasseur]] (French for "hunter"), almost indistinguishable from it, with [[shirvan]] and [[bakst-green]] a little greener [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a color near this swatch in 77 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.32 per cent, as photographed [2]. It is rare before 1900, then rises sharply in the 1910s, and is markedly over-represented among Post-Impressionist painters in our sample, including Paul Cézanne and Paul Gauguin [2]. Switzerland and the United States also show it above their average rates in our sample [2]. These are computed color matches to photographed, varnished paintings, not pigment identifications [2].
